newsitem.title: MALTA: Malta aims to raise status as finance centre.
newsitem.headline: Malta aims to raise status as finance centre.

text.p: Malta's central bank governor Francis Vassallo said he believed plans to make the Mediterranean island a financial centre would go ahead despite a change of government.
"The financial centre has the total commitment of the present government," said Vassallo.
The concept of making Malta such a centre was promoted by the government of the Nationalist Party, defeated in last weekend's general election.
But referring to 14 financial laws passed in 1994, Vassallo said: "They were unanimously approved in parliament so there is full support from this government in this context."

The Labour government's commitment to dismantle VAT, a basis of European Union membership, could mean Malta being a Switzerland of the Mediterranean, operating outside the EU, rather than a Luxembourg, operating within, he said.
The governor said he believed the project should be very successful. "I am speaking with great confidence because there is a total commitment of the existing government to this effect."

A major plank in the Labour election campaign was to remove VAT imposed in 1995 and to replace it with customs tariffs. It charged that VAT was brought in as part of the Nationalist Party's plans to take Malta into the EU and had brought hardship to the Maltese people.

Asked about disruption to the economy with the taxation change, Vassallo said: "It all depends on the timing. I think the political manifesto is very clear and it is just a question of the implementation, how it is carried out.
"And obviously the smoother it is carried out the better, the less shocks the economy will have."
